subject: Electrical Engineering
title: The Coulomb: Measuring Charge
description: Learn The Coulomb: Measuring Charge in one minute.

hook.text: One coulomb of charge is 6.24 quintillion electrons. A staggering number.

buildup.text: Charles-Augustin de Coulomb studied the force between charges in the 1780s.

discovery.text: Double the charge, quadruple the force. Double the distance, quarter the force.

twist.text: This inverse-square law mirrors gravity. Charge and mass follow the same math.

climax.text: Coulomb's law is the foundation of all electrostatics calculations.

punchline.text: Charge obeys the same rules as gravity — just far stronger.

quiz.question: What happens to the force when you double the distance between charges?
